title: Set up the project skeleton: folders, tooling, local environment and CI
body:
Create the empty-but-runnable foundation so the three of us can build server, client and GIS service in parallel without stepping on each other.

## What to build / rules
- Folders: `server/` (Express), `client/` (React: command dashboard + field app), `gis/` (Python GIS service), `db/` (migrations), `docs/`. These names are also used by the PR auto-labeler in `.github/labeler.yml`.
- TypeScript for server and client (team default), ESLint + Prettier with one shared config, `.editorconfig`, `.nvmrc`/Python version pin.
- `docker-compose.yml` that starts PostgreSQL with the PostGIS extension locally, plus `.env.example` for every package.
- Root README section 'Run locally' with the exact commands to start DB, server, client and GIS service.
- GitHub Actions CI on every PR: install, lint and test for each package that exists.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A fresh clone can be started by following the README only, with no extra steps
- [ ] `docker compose up db` gives a Postgres with PostGIS enabled (`SELECT postgis_version();` works)
- [ ] Each package has a 'hello world' that starts and one passing test
- [ ] CI runs on a test PR and is green; a PR touching `server/` gets the `area: backend` label automatically

## Out of scope
- Any product feature code
- Production deployment (separate decision)

**Priority:** P0 · **Size:** S

**Source:** Project proposal - technologies section

title: Design and create the PostgreSQL + PostGIS database schema (v1)
body:
Define every table the MVP needs, with the status enums from the decision log, so server and client work against one agreed data model.

## What to build / rules
- `missions`: name/ID, missing-person details (name, age, photo, description/clothing, disappearance time), status `Active|Paused|Ended`, end reason `Located|Stopped` + stop reason + note, join code, rally point (point geometry).
- `lkp_points`: many per mission, geometry + time + `is_current`; old points are kept (they are shown faded).
- `polygons`: geometry (Polygon, SRID 4326), name, status `Unassigned|Active|Completed`, cached coverage %, soft-delete (`deleted_at`) because routes and reports of deleted polygons must stay in history.
- `participants` (a phone-identified person inside one mission): name, phone, state `Available|Assigned|ActivityEnded`; the same phone can rejoin later with history preserved.
- `search_tasks`: participant + polygon + state `Assigned|Searching|Paused|FinishedSearch`, timestamps. A participant has at most one active task.
- `route_points`: task, point geometry, device time, server receive time, accuracy, battery, connectivity.
- `reports` (category, text, optional photo, geometry, time, status `New|Handled`, creator), `sightings` (location, time, short text, source `me|eyewitness`).
- `messages` + `message_deliveries` (level `Normal|Important|Critical`, scope mission/polygon/person, per-recipient `Sent|Read|Acknowledged`).
- `sos_events` (state `Active|Closed`, opener, location, optional message) and `mission_events` (significant-event timeline).
- Migration tool of your choice, spatial (GiST) indexes on all geometry columns, a seed script with one realistic demo mission.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Migrations run on an empty database and can be re-run safely in CI
- [ ] All status enums match the 'Statuses' sheet in the decision log exactly
- [ ] ERD committed in `docs/` and reviewed by all three team members
- [ ] Seed script produces a mission with polygons, searchers, routes and reports

#1

**Priority:** P0 · **Size:** L

**Source:** MVP Decision Log - statuses sheet, Q9, Q12, Q36, Q40, Q69-70

title: Build the Express API foundation: config, validation, errors, tests
body:
The shared backbone every endpoint will use, so each feature issue only adds routes and logic.

## What to build / rules
- Environment config validated at startup (fail fast with a clear message), structured request logging.
- Versioned routes under `/api/v1`, `/health` endpoint, CORS, JSON body limits.
- Request validation library (e.g. zod) and ONE error format: `{ error: { code, message, details? } }`.
- Realtime channel decision (WebSocket or Server-Sent Events) wired as a stub, because live monitoring, alerts and messaging all need it.
- Test setup (e.g. supertest) running against a throwaway Postgres schema; OpenAPI document generated from the routes.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `GET /api/v1/health` returns 200 with DB connectivity status
- [ ] An invalid request returns the standard error format with HTTP 400
- [ ] Tests run locally and in CI against a clean database
- [ ] A client can open the realtime channel and receive a test event

#1, #2

**Priority:** P0 · **Size:** M

**Source:** Project proposal - technologies section

title: Command accounts: sign up, log in, protect manager routes
body:
Managers (coordinators) get a basic account. Anyone with a Command account is an authorized manager who can create missions - there are no organizational roles in the MVP.

## What to build / rules
- Register, log in, log out, 'me' endpoint; passwords hashed (argon2 or bcrypt); session cookie or JWT with expiry.
- Auth middleware used by all manager-only endpoints; searcher (field) tokens must NOT be accepted there.
- Every Command account can create missions and manage the missions it created (single manager per mission in MVP).
- Login/registration screens in the dashboard (Hebrew, RTL).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A logged-out request to a manager endpoint returns 401
- [ ] A field-app token cannot call manager endpoints (403)
- [ ] After a browser refresh the manager stays logged in until the session expires
- [ ] Passwords are never logged or returned by any endpoint

## Depends on
#2, #3

## Out of scope
- Organization-level permissions and manager approval (see Future issues)
- Multiple managers per mission

**Priority:** P0 · **Size:** M

**Source:** MVP Decision Log Q50, Q51, Q67

title: Searcher sign-in with phone number and SMS code (OTP), persistent session
body:
Every searcher is identified by name and phone number verified with a one-time code. There is no anonymous guest mode. The session must survive closing and reopening the app.

## What to build / rules
- Flow: enter name + phone -> server sends OTP -> enter code -> session issued.
- OTP rules: short expiry, limited attempts, resend cooldown, rate-limit per phone and per IP.
- Session stored securely on the device (Keychain / Keystore); reopening the app returns the searcher to the state they were in (joined mission, assignment, searching).
- Development mode with a fixed code so the team can test without sending real SMS.
- SMS provider is chosen in the open decision issue; code the sender behind an interface so it can be swapped.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A new searcher can sign in with phone + code and appears with name and phone in the mission roster
- [ ] Closing and reopening the app keeps the session without asking for a code again
- [ ] Wrong or expired code is rejected; repeated attempts are throttled
- [ ] No endpoint accepts an unauthenticated searcher

#2, #3, #42

## Out of scope
- Guest / anonymous join (explicitly removed from MVP)

title: Shared map layer: OpenStreetMap tiles, place search and coordinate input
body:
One reusable map component and geocoding service for the dashboard and the field app, used for LKP, Rally Point, polygons, tracking and reports.

## What to build / rules
- Map renders OSM-based tiles with pan/zoom, markers, polygons and lines; Hebrew labels display correctly in RTL layout.
- Search box for addresses and places; separate input that accepts raw coordinates (e.g. `32.0853, 34.7818`).
- Click-on-map selection returns lat/lng.
- Provider hidden behind a small interface so tiles/geocoding can be replaced; respect OSM tile-usage policy (do not hammer the public tile server - plan caching or a tile provider).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Searching for a known place centers the map and offers a pin
- [ ] Typing valid coordinates places a pin; invalid input shows an inline error
- [ ] Component is used by the dashboard first and is reusable by the field app

title: Create a mission: form, validation and automatic activation
body:
The coordinator opens a new search mission by entering the basic operational information. The mission becomes Active immediately - there is no draft state.

## What to build / rules
- Fields: mission name/ID, missing person's details, photo, description/clothing, disappearance time, LKP (Last Known Position) and any relevant info.
- Rally Point is mandatory (selected with the map tools from the LKP/Rally Point issue); the form cannot be submitted without it.
- On submit: mission is created as `Active`, a join code + QR + link are generated, the manager lands on the live mission screen.
- Server-side validation mirrors the form; photo upload with size/type limits.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A manager can create a mission with all fields and sees it Active right away
- [ ] Submitting without LKP or Rally Point is blocked with a clear message
- [ ] The created mission shows its join code, QR and share link
- [ ] A `mission created` event appears in the timeline

## Depends on
#2, #3, #4, #6, #8

## Out of scope
- Draft missions
- Multiple managers

**Priority:** P0 · **Size:** M

**Source:** MVP Decision Log Q1, Q66, Q91

title: LKP and Rally Point: set, update, keep history, propagate to the field
body:
Two critical map points: the Last Known Position (where the person was last seen) and the Rally Point (the gathering place). Both can be set three ways and updated during the mission.

## What to build / rules
- Set by: clicking the map, searching an address/place, or typing coordinates.
- LKP history: when the LKP changes, old points are kept, shown faded; the current one is highlighted.
- The system may SUGGEST turning a sighting into the new LKP; the manager always decides (hook for the Sightings issue).
- Rally Point is mandatory and editable at any time. Online devices get the change immediately; offline devices get it at next sync. Same for a new LKP.
- Every change is recorded in the mission timeline.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Manager can set LKP and Rally Point with all three methods
- [ ] Changing the LKP keeps the old one (faded) and highlights the new one
- [ ] A connected field device sees the new Rally Point within seconds; an offline device sees it after reconnecting
- [ ] Mission cannot exist without a Rally Point

## Depends on
#2, #6

## Out of scope
- Automatic LKP calculation (the V1 probability layer builds on this later)

**Priority:** P0 · **Size:** M

title: Search polygons: draw, edit, delete, overlap, immediate use
body:
The manager divides the search area by drawing polygons by hand. Each polygon is an independent unit of work that searchers are assigned to.

## What to build / rules
- Draw/edit vertices on the map, name and color each polygon. No hierarchy (no 'search area -> sectors') in MVP.
- Overlapping polygons are allowed on purpose (operational choice); show overlap clearly.
- A new polygon is immediately assignable; only people assigned to a polygon get notified about changes to it.
- Editing: when a saved change would put currently-searching people outside the new boundary, show a warning before saving and notify them after saving.
- Deleting removes the polygon from the active view but keeps its routes and reports in mission history.
- Status lives separately from coverage: `Unassigned -> Active -> Completed`, with its own Coverage %.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Manager can draw, rename, edit and delete polygons and sees them on the map
- [ ] Overlapping polygons are accepted
- [ ] Editing a boundary while searchers are inside shows the warning and sends the notification after save
- [ ] After deleting a polygon its historical routes and reports are still visible in history

## Depends on
#2, #3, #6

## Out of scope
- Automatic/AI polygon suggestions
- Sector hierarchy and Sector Leader role

**Priority:** P0 · **Size:** L

**Source:** MVP Decision Log Q3, Q4, Q12, Q35-Q38

title: Joining a mission: code, QR, link, duplicate join and rejoin
body:
How a volunteer gets into a mission and what happens in the edge cases.

## What to build / rules
- Each mission has one join code plus a QR and a link that open the same join flow.
- After joining the searcher is `Available` in the pool; the manager assigns them - searchers never pick a polygon themselves.
- Joining is allowed only while the mission is Active (not when Paused or Ended).
- Joining twice with the same phone returns the existing participation, no duplicate.
- A searcher who ended their activity can rejoin; history is kept and they return to Available for a new assignment.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Code, QR and link all lead to the same mission
- [ ] A second join with the same phone does not create a duplicate participant
- [ ] Joining a Paused or Ended mission shows a clear message and is blocked
- [ ] Rejoin after Finish Activity works and keeps previous routes and reports in history

#2, #3, #5

**Priority:** P0 · **Size:** M

**Source:** MVP Decision Log Q6, Q7, Q47, Q69, Q70, Q82, Q83

title: Assigning searchers to polygons: assign, reassign, one task at a time
body:
The manager sees the pool of available searchers and gives each one a polygon.

## What to build / rules
- A polygon can have one searcher or several. A searcher has at most ONE active search task.
- Manager-only action; the searcher is notified of the new assignment.
- Reassigning: the old task ends, the transit between polygons is NOT counted as searching, and the searcher must press Start Search again manually for the new polygon.
- Roster view shows for each person: name, phone, status, current polygon.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Manager can assign an Available searcher to any polygon and the searcher is notified
- [ ] Trying to give a searcher a second active task is rejected
- [ ] After reassignment the old task is closed and the new one starts only when the searcher taps Start Search
- [ ] Assignment changes appear in the timeline

## Depends on
#9, #10

## Out of scope
- Self-selection of polygons by searchers

**Priority:** P0 · **Size:** M

**Source:** MVP Decision Log Q5, Q7, Q28, Q40

title: Mission lifecycle: pause, resume, stop, and person-located
body:
The mission-level state machine and what each transition does to the people in the field.

## What to build / rules
- States: `Active <-> Paused`, and ended as either `Located` (missing person found) or `Stopped` (search called off).
- Pause: searchers stop searching and return to the Rally Point; tracking continues until each person presses Finish Activity.
- Resume: assignments are preserved; every searcher must press Start Search again.
- End (either way): the search ends but safety tracking continues until Finish Activity.
- Stop requires a reason chosen from a list plus an optional note. Located records location + time with an optional note, and is only set by the manager after verification.
- All transitions notify the field and are written to the timeline.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Each transition is possible only from the allowed states and is enforced on the server
- [ ] Pausing sends searchers a clear instruction to go to the Rally Point
- [ ] After Resume nobody is automatically 'Searching' until they tap Start Search
- [ ] Ended missions keep tracking safety data until each participant finishes activity

title: Edit mission details and push relevant changes to searchers
body:
The manager can correct or extend the missing-person information during the mission; searchers see it read-only.

## What to build / rules
- Editable: missing-person details, photo, description/clothing, other relevant info.
- Changes sync to the field app; offline devices receive them at next connection.
- A 'significant change' (team to confirm the list in this issue, e.g. clothing, photo, last-seen time, medical condition) also creates an alert in the field app.
- Searchers can never edit this information.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Manager edit appears in a connected field app within seconds
- [ ] A significant change raises an alert; a minor one only updates silently
- [ ] Edit history appears in the timeline

title: Field app foundation: join, waiting state, assignment view
body:
The searcher's app shell: everything a volunteer sees from joining until they start searching.

## What to build / rules
- Screens: sign-in (phone/OTP), join (code / QR scan / link), waiting for assignment (Available), assignment view with the polygon on the map, read-only missing-person details, mission-status banner (Paused / Ended).
- Privacy: before and during search the searcher does NOT see other searchers' locations or routes.
- Hebrew-first, RTL, large touch targets (used outdoors, possibly with gloves, in bright light).
- Needs UX design before build (see `needs-design`).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A new user can go from install to seeing their assigned polygon without help
- [ ] No screen shows other searchers' positions or routes
- [ ] Mission Paused / Ended banners appear immediately when the state changes
- [ ] Layout verified in RTL on small and large phones

#5, #6, #10

- Tracking and reports (separate issues)

**Priority:** P0 · **Size:** L

**Source:** MVP Decision Log Q31-Q33

title: Searcher status flow: start, pause, resume, finish search
body:
The searcher-side state machine that drives tracking and coverage.

## What to build / rules
- States: `Available -> Assigned -> Searching <-> Paused -> Finished Search`.
- After assignment the searcher taps Start Search; only then GPS route recording and coverage begin.
- Finish Search ends only the search task. The person stays Assigned to the same polygon until the manager decides what's next, and the polygon is NOT marked completed - only the manager completes polygons.
- Personal pause: tracking continues for safety but does not contribute to coverage until resume.
- Start is blocked until required permissions and offline-map readiness are satisfied.
- The server validates every transition.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Invalid transitions are rejected by the server
- [ ] Finish Search leaves the polygon status unchanged and the searcher still assigned
- [ ] While personally paused, route points are stored but excluded from coverage
- [ ] Start Search is disabled with an explanation when permissions or offline maps are missing

#11, #14, #16, #28

**Priority:** P0 · **Size:** M

**Source:** MVP Decision Log Q8-Q10, Q71, Q85, Q100

title: Background GPS tracking and permission flow (iOS + Android)
body:
Reliable route recording even when the screen is locked or another app is open - the core of safety monitoring and coverage.

## What to build / rules
- Continuous tracking in background / locked screen; battery-aware sampling (interval is an engineering choice, documented).
- Permissions: location (required before Start Search), notifications (required), camera (NOT required; asked only when the searcher takes a photo for a report, and reporting without photo must work).
- Joining and viewing is allowed without permissions; Start Search is blocked until granted, with a clear explanation screen.
- If GPS is unavailable: the searcher is warned, the manager sees 'GPS unavailable', and time without GPS is not counted as search time.
- Each route point stores accuracy, battery and connectivity for the manager's live view.
- Platform background-location limits are researched in the providers decision issue.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] On both iOS and Android, tracking keeps recording for 30+ minutes with screen locked (manual test log attached)
- [ ] Denied permissions block Start Search but not join/view
- [ ] Turning GPS off shows the warning to the searcher and 'unavailable' to the manager
- [ ] Route points reach the server with accuracy and battery fields

#14, #42

title: Manager live monitoring: map and roster of active searchers
body:
The coordinator's real-time picture of the field.

## What to build / rules
- Map markers + side roster showing for each searcher: position, polygon, status, route trail, last-update time, connectivity (Online/Offline), battery.
- Updates pushed in real time over the realtime channel.
- If the app is force-closed or silent, the manager keeps seeing the last update time; after the 'lost contact' threshold (open decision) the searcher is marked 'lost contact'.
- Filter by polygon and status; clicking a marker opens the person's details and call button.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A moving test phone appears and updates on the dashboard within a few seconds
- [ ] Last update, connectivity and battery are visible per searcher
- [ ] A silent device is flagged as lost contact after the configured threshold
- [ ] Roster remains usable with 50 simulated searchers

#3, #16, #38

**Priority:** P0 · **Size:** L

**Source:** MVP Decision Log Q13, Q44, Q45

title: Alert when a searcher leaves their polygon
body:
Detect and report boundary exits so coverage stays reliable and people stay safe.

## What to build / rules
- While Searching, if a person's position is outside their assigned polygon, BOTH the searcher and the manager are alerted.
- Tolerance around the border (to avoid false alarms from GPS noise) is defined in the open decision issue; implement it as a configurable constant.
- De-bounce: require several consecutive outside fixes; the alert clears automatically when the person returns.
- Event appears in the manager's feed and timeline.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Walking out of a test polygon triggers alerts on both screens; walking back clears them
- [ ] A single noisy GPS point does not trigger an alert
- [ ] Tolerance value can be changed in one place

## Depends on
#9, #16, #39, #27

**Priority:** P1 · **Size:** M

**Source:** MVP Decision Log Q14

title: Coverage engine: estimate how much of each polygon was searched
body:
Automatic estimate of searched area per polygon, combining the routes of everyone who worked in it.

## What to build / rules
- Cumulative: routes from several searchers and several sessions are merged into one coverage per polygon.
- A route only contributes to the polygon the person was ASSIGNED to at the time it was recorded; only the part physically inside that polygon counts (the rest is kept in history).
- Excluded: time while paused, without GPS, or after Finish Search.
- Coverage % is automatic only - the manager cannot type a percentage. It is shown next to the polygon's status.
- Parameters (search width/buffer, sampling, GPS-jump filtering) come from the coverage algorithm decision issue.
- Draw the covered area as a map overlay; update incrementally, not by recomputing everything.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A scripted test walk of a known path produces the expected coverage within a stated tolerance
- [ ] Two searchers covering the same ground do not double-count
- [ ] A route outside the assigned polygon does not increase coverage
- [ ] Coverage updates on the dashboard within seconds of new points

title: Manager marks a polygon as Completed
body:
Closing out a polygon is a manager decision, independent of the coverage percentage.

## What to build / rules
- Manager can mark a polygon Completed at any coverage %.
- After confirmation: all search tasks in that polygon end, assigned searchers are notified, and they return to the pool (Available).
- Routes and coverage are preserved and keep accumulating if more data arrives.
- Recorded in the timeline.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Completing a polygon notifies and releases all its searchers
- [ ] Coverage and routes of a completed polygon remain visible
- [ ] Completed status is shown on map and roster

title: Field reports: create a report with category, text, photo and location
body:
Searchers send findings from the field to the manager.

## What to build / rules
- Five main report categories (the decision log fixes the number; final category names are set during UX design in this issue).
- Content: free text, optional photo, GPS location and time attached automatically.
- Camera permission requested only when attaching a photo; a report without photo must always be possible.
- Works offline: queued locally and sent on reconnect.
- A searcher sees only reports from their own polygon plus their own reports - never other polygons.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A report with text only, and a report with photo, both reach the manager with correct location and time
- [ ] Creating a report offline delivers it after reconnecting, exactly once
- [ ] A searcher cannot see reports from polygons they are not assigned to

title: Report handling for managers: map + list, status, edit and delete
body:
How the coordinator triages the incoming flow of reports.

## What to build / rules
- Reports shown both on the map and in a list; new ones highlighted and notified.
- Status flow `New -> Handled`, set by the manager.
- Edit: manager or the creator can edit; there is no version history.
- Delete: manager only.
- Filters by category, polygon, status.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Manager sees a new report appear live on map and list
- [ ] Marking Handled updates both views
- [ ] Only manager can delete; creator can edit own report; non-creator searcher cannot

title: 'Person located' report: critical alert flow
body:
The most important event in a mission gets its own flow.

## What to build / rules
- A searcher can submit a Located report with location + time and an optional note.
- It triggers a CRITICAL alert to the manager (sound/vibration, persistent until acknowledged).
- The mission does NOT end automatically: only the manager ends it, after verifying (uses the lifecycle issue).
- Manager can broadcast instructions to the field right from the alert.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Submitting a Located report raises a critical alert on the manager's dashboard immediately
- [ ] The mission stays Active until the manager ends it
- [ ] Alert is recorded in the timeline with who/where/when

title: Sightings: record where someone may have seen the missing person
body:
A sighting is a lightweight lead (different from a field report) that appears on the map and can feed the LKP.

## What to build / rules
- Both manager and searcher can create a sighting.
- Fields: location, time, short description, source (`me` / `eyewitness`). Certainty level and photo are NOT in MVP.
- In MVP a sighting shows on the map immediately (verification step is a Future item).
- From a sighting the manager can accept the system's suggestion to make it the new LKP.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Sighting created by a searcher or manager appears on all relevant maps
- [ ] 'Make this the LKP' works and keeps the previous LKP in history
- [ ] Sightings are available as input for the V1 probability layer later

## Depends on
#2, #8, #14

- Verification before a sighting becomes operational (Future)

**Priority:** P1 · **Size:** M

**Source:** MVP Decision Log Q59-Q63

title: Manager broadcast messages with levels and delivery tracking
body:
One-way announcements from the manager to the field (no chat).

## What to build / rules
- Recipients: the whole mission, one polygon, or one individual.
- Levels: Normal / Important / Critical; free text or ready templates.
- Delivery tracking: Normal = Sent -> Read; Critical = Sent -> Read -> Acknowledged (searcher must tap to confirm). Manager sees per-recipient status.
- Messages to offline devices are stored and delivered on reconnect, keeping the same states.
- Field inbox screen; Important/Critical also via push notification.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A message to a polygon reaches only its searchers
- [ ] A critical message shows as unacknowledged until each recipient confirms
- [ ] A message sent while a device is offline arrives after reconnect with correct states

## Depends on
#3, #14, #27

## Out of scope
- Two-way chat

**Priority:** P0 · **Size:** L

**Source:** MVP Decision Log Q25-Q27, Q77

title: SOS button and phone calling
body:
Emergency escalation from the field.

## What to build / rules
- Searcher presses SOS: the manager receives their identity + location, with an optional short message.
- The alert goes to the manager AND all searchers in the same polygon.
- Closed by the searcher who opened it or by the manager; updates are sent to all recipients. States: `Active -> Closed`.
- A Call button opens the standard phone dialer for the manager; during SOS the emergency-services number is shown prominently next to it.
- Manager's number is available during the whole mission.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Pressing SOS shows an alert with name and location on the manager's dashboard and on same-polygon phones
- [ ] Closing the SOS sends an update to all recipients
- [ ] Call buttons open the system dialer with the correct number

#14, #27, #16

**Priority:** P0 · **Size:** L

**Source:** MVP Decision Log Q24, Q78, Q79, Q98, Q99

title: Push notifications: device registration and priority delivery
body:
The delivery infrastructure used by messages, SOS, boundary alerts and the located alert.

## What to build / rules
- Register device tokens per signed-in user (iOS and Android); remove on sign-out.

title: Offline-first data: store GPS and reports locally, sync automatically
body:
Searchers keep working with no signal; nothing is lost.

## What to build / rules
- While offline: GPS route points and reports are stored locally.
- On reconnect: automatic upload, idempotent (client-generated IDs, so a retry never duplicates), ordered by device time.
- While a searcher is offline, the manager cannot change their active task or directly-related info (prevents conflicts).
- LKP and Rally Point changes made meanwhile reach the device at next connection; queued messages follow.
- Visible sync status in the app (pending count, last sync).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Recording a 20-minute offline route and reconnecting uploads all points once, in order
- [ ] Offline report arrives exactly once after reconnect
- [ ] Manager UI blocks changes to an offline searcher's active task with an explanation
- [ ] Killing the app mid-offline does not lose stored data
